description: Get World Bank time-series data — economic, social, and development statistics — for ANY country worldwide (Spain, Brazil, Germany, Nigeria, Japan, etc.). PREFER for "unemployment rate in <country>", "<country> inflation rate", "GDP of <country>", "<country> population / life expectancy / poverty rate / CO2 emissions", "what share of GDP comes from agriculture in <country>" / "agriculture's share of GDP". Pass the ISO country code + a World Bank indicator code; common ones: GDP=NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, GDP per capita=NY.GDP.PCAP.CD, inflation=FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, unemployment=SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS, population=SP.POP.TOTL, life expectancy=SP.DYN.LE00.IN, poverty rate=SI.POV.DDAY, literacy=SE.ADT.LITR.ZS, agriculture value added (% of GDP)=NV.AGR.TOTL.ZS. For CO2 use the dedicated country_co2_emissions tool (the old EN.ATM.CO2E.* codes were DELETED by the World Bank; the live series is EN.GHG.CO2.MT.CE.AR5). For governance/corruption/rule-of-law/political-stability use the dedicated get_governance_indicators tool (Worldwide Governance Indicators, codes like GOV_WGI_CC.EST). Several countries over time in one call ("cereal yield in Brazil, Argentina and the US over the past decade", "inflation in Spain vs Italy since 2015"): pass up to 8 codes separated by ";" — each country comes back as its own series. Agriculture: cereal yield (kg per hectare)=AG.YLD.CREL.KG. (Annual data — a national statistics office may have fresher monthly figures.)

country_code.description: ISO country code (e.g., "US", "GBR", "CN"). For a multi-country comparison over time pass up to 8 codes separated by ";" (e.g., "US;BR;AR") — one series per country.

name: worldbank_get_indicator
